decision: Adopt a two-PDF partial-density colour-gradient (f = species-A partial density, g = species-B partial density, rho = rho_A + rho_B, phi = (rho_A-rho_B)/rho) as the library's mass-exact two-phase colour-gradient engine and validate it against the closed-form two-layer Poiseuille solution and the Laplace law.
alternatives: A1 (chosen): two-PDF partial density, BGK tau(phi) from harmonic viscosity interpolation, Guo(2002) forcing, Latva-Kokko/Rothman isotropic recolouring (beta), anisotropic colour-gradient perturbation for surface tension. New additive module src/tensorlbm/color_gradient_two_pdf.py, stock modules untouched.

A2: literal MF-LBM recolouring stencil (main axes 4/9, diagonals 1/(36 sqrt 2)) at the same amplitude scaling -> REJECTED on measured evidence: drives the minority partial density negative (min rho_sigma = -0.11, ny=32, 1000 steps, artifacts/recolour_stencil_probe.json).
A3: keep the existing single-PDF two-component two-tau engine (tensorlbm.color_gradient2d) only -> rejected as the target of this anchor (it is used here as an independent cross-model check instead).

A4: CSF (continuum surface force) surface tension as in MF-LBM (0.5*gamma*kappa*|C|*n in moment space) -> deferred: perturbation form keeps the change minimal and is validated by the Laplace law; recorded as a design deviation.

external_anchor.analytic_1: two-layer stratified Poiseuille, u'' = -g/nu per layer, no slip at the half-way planes Y=0.5 and ny-1.5, velocity and shear-stress continuity at Y_i = j_first_blue - 0.5 (frozen evaluator cg_reference.py, md5 e78c6d1eb22d628182636c0df74fb26a)
external_anchor.analytic_2: Laplace law dp = sigma / R for a static droplet (radius independence of sigma = dp*R)
